text:
Matt Maddock urges action on utility spending and calls for increased voter participation
P. P. Cantu
Matt Maddock, a Michigan state representative, used his Twitter account in early August 2026 to address issues related to political spending by utility companies, tax burdens, and voter participation.
On August 2, 2026, Maddock criticized the involvement of utility companies in politics. He stated, "DTE and Consumers pour tens of millions of ratepayer money into politics. Sept 24 is the deadline for the Legislature to vote to stop this scam. Call your state legislators. Tell them to vote yes. I’m all in on this. Are you?" DTE Energy and Consumers Energy are two major utility providers in Michigan that have faced scrutiny over their political contributions.
The following day, on August 3, 2026, Maddock addressed concerns about taxation levels compared to basic living expenses: "We now pay more in taxes than we do for housing, food and clothing. We don’t have an affordability problem, we have a big-government problem." This statement reflects ongoing debates about government spending and tax policy at both state and national levels.
On August 4, 2026, Maddock commented on voter engagement: "It’s one of the saddest things. A lot of people don’t vote because they feel they don’t know enough about politics… so in their heads, they just leave it to the people who do. Call your friends who don’t vote and tell them to vote." Voter turnout has been a recurring issue in U.S. elections; efforts by public officials often focus on increasing participation among eligible voters.
Maddock's remarks highlight persistent topics within Michigan politics—utility regulation, taxation policies, and civic engagement—which continue to generate discussion among lawmakers and constituents.
